target.title: fix(line): record every LINE push message id in send receipts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE send receipts discarded all returned LINE message ids and mislabeled multi-part sends. `pushLineMessages` returned a hardcoded `messageId: "push"` and `sendMessageLine`'s reply branch returned `"reply"` while discarding the response, so neither path recorded a real id. A single send can produce several messages — media + caption is two, one `sentMessages[].id` each — and every returned id was dropped from the receipt. The receipt also stamped one aggregate `kind` on every id, recording a media + caption send as `[media, media]` instead of `[media, text]`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`@line/bot-sdk` 11.1.0 types the `sentMessages` response as 1–5 items (`minItems: 1`), one per submitted message, for both push (`PushMessageResponse`) and reply (`ReplyMessageResponse`), and LINE guarantees the array order matches the sent message objects ([LINE docs](https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/get-quote-tokens/): "the order of the elements in the `sentMessages` array is guaranteed to be the same as the order of the message objects when they were sent"). Push discarded that response; reply never captured it. Because a successful response carries at least one id (`minItems: 1`), the removed `"push"` / `"reply"` were placeholders, not ids; handling a malformed empty response is separate hardening and out of scope.

Push and reply now share one ordered receipt path (`buildLineSendResult`): the first returned id stays the singular `messageId`, every id is recorded as an ordered `parts` entry, and each id is keyed to its own kind via the documented order (`sentMessages[i]` ↔ `messages[i]`), so a media + caption send records `[media, text]`. Both paths share the same broken receipt invariant; recording ids without their kinds, or fixing one path and not the other, leaves the receipt half-correct, so they land together.

The per-message kind is carried on each flat receipt-input result (an additive optional `kind`), not a separate parallel array, so each id and its kind travel together and cannot be misaligned on the exported helper (which no longer takes a separate `kinds` array). The shared normalizer already owns id-dedup, primary-id derivation, and part/`sentAt` assembly and only accepted one uniform `kind`; the alternative — LINE building the `MessageReceipt` itself — would fork all of that into the plugin and drift from the shared shape. Carrying the kind per result keeps one receipt builder, touches no existing caller (results without a `kind` fall back to the uniform `kind`; nested-receipt adapters are unchanged), keeps `kind` out of the raw platform result, and adds no new receipt shape (`platformMessageIds`, `parts`, `primaryPlatformMessageId` already model ordered multi-id receipts). "One physical message carries its own kind" is a generic receipt property, not LINE-specific.

Scope (5 files): LINE response capture + receipt construction (`send.ts`, `send-receipt.ts`), one additive core normalizer option (`receipt.ts`), and the two focused test files.

## User Impact

Consumers of LINE send receipts get the real LINE message id for every sent message, on push and on reply. The receipt schema is unchanged: `messageId` / `primaryPlatformMessageId` change value (real id instead of a `"push"` / `"reply"` placeholder), and `platformMessageIds` / `parts` change cardinality — a media + caption send now exposes both ordered ids (one `parts` entry each) with kinds `[media, text]`.

## Evidence

**Tests** — `pnpm test extensions/line` (26 files, 310 tests passed) and `pnpm test src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts` pass. A media + caption reply asserts both ids in order with kinds `[media, text]` and the first primary; the media + caption push asserts the same order plus `parts[].kind === [media, text]`; a normalizer case asserts each flat result's own `kind` applies with aggregate-kind fallback and stays out of `raw`. `tsgo`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` are clean; GitHub CI is green on this head.

**Manual credential-backed proof (exact head `a4a1c5ccd2de07679fca6c73a5977aff5c71d92b`)** — a `node --import tsx` script drives the production `sendMessageLine` path against the real LINE Messaging API with a real channel access token, for a media + caption send LINE delivers as two messages, on both push and reply (reply token captured live from an inbound webhook event). Redacted terminal output showing the live provider round-trip and the resulting receipt (real ids truncated to `…`):

```
[capture] inbound message; replyToken 4d46…90 captured.
[real LINE API] POST api.line.me/v2/bot/message/reply -> 200 sentMessages=["6224…46", "6224…30"]
  REPLY: platformMessageIds=["6224…46", "6224…30"]  parts.kind=[media, text]  messageId=6224…46  => PASS
[real LINE API] POST api.line.me/v2/bot/message/push  -> 200 sentMessages=["6224…98", "6224…97"]
  PUSH:  platformMessageIds=["6224…98", "6224…97"]  parts.kind=[media, text]  messageId=6224…98  => PASS

OVERALL: reply=PASS push=PASS
```

Each path asserts `platformMessageIds` equals both returned ids in order, `messageId`/`primaryPlatformMessageId` equals the first, and — via LINE's documented `sentMessages` order — `parts[].kind` equals `[media, text]`. On current `main` the same paths return the literal `"push"` / `"reply"`; reverting the `send.ts` mapping reproduces the placeholder.
